head: The Canadiens are on a heater
paras: The Penguins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-5 in overtime in Pittsburgh on Oct 3. The Canadiens have won four straight, while the Pens (5-6-2) lost 4-3 in overtime to Utah on Thursday. Going in, the Penguins are sixth in the Metropolitan (24th in the NHL) and the Canadiens second in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.462) says: their chances are worth about .562, and losses in one-goal games have held them back. The Canadiens’ record (.692) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.567), largely thanks to winning one-goal games.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck, get more of their shots from in close than anyone and rarely throw hits. The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone, give up more power plays than they draw and have struggled on the power play, scoring on 10.3% of their chances (third worst). That means the Penguins could find some good looks against the Canadiens, who give up plenty of them. Beyond that, the Canadiens have the edge over the Penguins on forecheck pressure.

Erik Karlsson (2 G / 11 A / 13 P in 13 GP) is carrying the Penguins’ offense, and Evgeni Malkin (6 G / 5 A / 11 P in 12 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Canadiens, Cole Caufield (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Lane Hutson (3 G / 8 A / 11 P in 13 GP) is next in line.
Artūrs Šilovs (5-3-1 / .889 SV% in 9 GS) should get the start for Pittsburgh, and Jacob Fowler (6-1-0 / .942 SV% in 7 GS) for Montréal.

items.text: The Penguins are newly without Bryan Rust, and have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk since Oct 9.
The Canadiens are newly without Mike Matheson, and have been without Nick Suzuki, Samuel Montembeault and Ivan Demidov for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
Phillip Danault is set to play his 800th NHL game.
Chris Kreider has six goals in nine games against Pittsburgh since 2023-24, most of them with the Rangers.

MTL.head: Anybody’s game
MTL.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, the Canadiens will be without Suzuki. On top of that, Pittsburgh gets Solovyov back. The Canadiens can tip it if they get good looks.

PIT.head: A genuine toss-up
PIT.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Pittsburgh gets Solovyov back. On top of that, Montréal will be without Suzuki. The Penguins can tip it if they get good looks.

calls.head: No wasted shots for the Penguins
calls.body: When the Penguins shoot, it’s usually a real chance, and the Canadiens are one of the league’s worst at stopping that. Jacob Fowler is going to be busy in all the wrong ways.

calls.head: The Canadiens’ edge in forecheck pressure
calls.body: The Canadiens are around the middle of the league for forecheck pressure, and the Penguins are the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
